full_judgment: 4. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioner submits that Section 18 of the Stamp Act, having provided that three months after it has been first received in Bangladesh and it is taken to the Collector, he shall stamp the same the Deputy Commissioner had legal obligation to revalidate the power of attorney and the High Court Division committed an error of law in not holding that the refusal by the Deputy Commissioner to revalidate the power of attorney has been done without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. Mr. Bhuiyan further submits that the power of attorney executed outside Bangladesh, attested by Notary Public of that country and authenticated by Bangladesh High Commission in that country has a presumption of validity and that presumption not having been rebutted and the original owners are the aggrieved parties and not their .attorney in that the attorney filed the writ petition for enforcement of his own authority to act as attorney and therefore, he is an aggrieved party within the meaning of Article 102 of . the Constitution; the High Court Division having found that the execution and authentication of the document in question cannot be disputed and that there cannot be any dispute as regard execution and authentication of the power of attorney, thereby committed an error of law in not giving the direction to the Deputy Commissioner to revalidate the power of attorney; that the power of attorney having specifically mentioned the Mouzas in which the lands of the principal is situated and as the attorney while performing his function as attorney will have to produce papers in respect of the lands owned by the principal, the Deputy Commissioner wrongly refused to revalidate the power of attorney; that when in the schedule to the power of attorney the names of mouzas in which the lands of the principal have been situated have been mentioned the learned Judges of the High Court Division was not right in observing that an unspecified schedule has been appended to the, power of attorney; that the High Court Division committed an error of law in holding that the writ petition is not maintainable in that the attorney has authority to act as agent of the principal and therefore, he has sufficient interest to maintain the writ petition. Lastly, Mr. Bhuiyan further submits that the High Court Division committed an error of law in holding that since the order of refusal passed by the Deputy Commissioner was not challenged and a direction, was sought to the Deputy Commissioner to revalidate the power of attorney the writ petition is not maintainable in that if the direction is given to the Deputy Commissioner it would mean that the order of the Deputy Commissioner has been passed without lawful authority.
